title: Electromagnetic Waves: The Spectrum That Carries the Modern World

questions.question: Electromagnetic waves differ from sound waves in that they:
questions.rationale: EM waves are self-sustaining oscillations of electric and magnetic fields and need no medium — they cross vacuum at 3 × 10⁸ m/s, which sound cannot do.

questions.question: Arrange these in order of increasing frequency: I. X-rays, II. Radio waves, III. Green light, IV. Infrared.
questions.rationale: Frequency rises from radio → infrared → visible → X-rays, since c = fλ fixes high frequency with short wavelength.

questions.question: The energy of a photon is given by:
questions.rationale: Each photon carries E = hf, where h is Planck's constant — so higher frequency means a more energetic photon.

questions.question: Why do gamma rays damage living tissue while radio waves do not?
options: Gamma-ray photons carry enough energy to ionise atoms and break molecular bonds
Radio waves are too weak to exist
questions.rationale: Ionising radiation has photons energetic enough (E = hf) to strip electrons from atoms and damage DNA; low-frequency photons cannot.

questions.question: A microwave oven heats food mainly by making which molecules oscillate?
questions.rationale: Microwaves at ~2.45 GHz flip polar water molecules back and forth billions of times a second; friction between molecules then converts this motion into heat.

questions.question: The sky appears blue because:
options: Air molecules scatter short (blue) wavelengths far more strongly than long ones
The Sun emits mostly blue light
questions.rationale: Rayleigh scattering varies as 1/λ⁴, so blue light is scattered around the sky much more than red; at sunset the long path leaves reds to reach our eyes.

questions.question: X-ray and gamma-ray astronomy must be done from satellites because:
options: These waves move too fast for ground telescopes
Earth's atmosphere absorbs X-rays and gamma rays
The Moon blocks them from the ground
questions.rationale: The atmosphere is opaque to ionising radiation — fortunate for life on the surface, but it means observatories like Chandra must orbit above it.

questions.question: An EM wave of wavelength 3 m has a frequency of about:
questions.rationale: f = c/λ = (3 × 10⁸)/(3) = 10⁸ Hz = 100 MHz — an FM radio band frequency.

questions.question: Radar measures an aircraft's distance by:
options: Timing the echo of a reflected microwave pulse
questions.rationale: Radar sends a microwave pulse and times the echo; distance = c × (time)/2, while the Doppler shift of the echo gives speed.

questions.question: Which pair of colours brackets the visible spectrum?
questions.rationale: Visible light spans roughly 700 nm (red) to 400 nm (violet), flanked by infrared on the long side and ultraviolet on the short side.
